examples.scenario: Raw GNSS ellipsoidal height is labelled ODN.
examples.reason: Ellipsoidal height and ODN orthometric height are different vertical coordinates.

examples.scenario: ODN height is fed back as ellipsoidal height.
examples.reason: Target orthometric height cannot silently become ellipsoid height.

examples.scenario: EPSG:5701 is omitted and only metre units are recorded.
examples.reason: Equal units do not prove equal vertical datum.

examples.scenario: British National Grid easting/northing are combined with an unspecified height datum.
examples.reason: Horizontal CRS alone does not define the height reference.

examples.scenario: EPSG:7405 is replaced by EPSG:27700 while retaining height values.
examples.reason: EPSG:27700 has no ODN vertical component.

examples.scenario: OSTN15 is used and assumed to convert height.
examples.reason: OSTN15 is horizontal; OSGM15 handles height.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 is skipped because coordinates are already in British National Grid.
examples.reason: Horizontal coordinate frame does not imply ODN height conversion was applied.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 full 1 km grid is replaced by the 20 km Lite pack.
examples.reason: The reduced-density pack is lower-accuracy and not the full terminal model.

examples.scenario: A nearest-neighbour OSGM15 grid lookup replaces bilinear interpolation.
examples.reason: OS documents bilinear interpolation for location-specific separation values.

examples.scenario: Only one OSGM15 node is stored for replay.
examples.reason: Bilinear replay requires the surrounding grid-node set and weights.

examples.scenario: OSGM02 result is accepted because it differs by only centimetres.
examples.reason: OSGM02 was superseded by OSGM15 and cannot silently substitute.

examples.scenario: EPSG:10021 is selected instead of EPSG:7711.
examples.reason: EPSG:10021 represents the superseded OSGM02 operation.

examples.scenario: Model filename matches but file bytes differ.
examples.reason: Filename equality is insufficient for exact transformation provenance.

examples.scenario: PROJ uses uk_os_OSGM15_GB.tif while the manifest references another regional grid.
examples.reason: Regional resource identity must match target location.

examples.scenario: Mainland ODN is applied to a Lerwick target.
examples.reason: OSGM15 contains regional datums that are not interchangeable.

examples.scenario: Mainland ODN is applied to Stornoway.
examples.reason: Outer Hebrides use a distinct regional datum.

examples.scenario: Mainland ODN is applied to Douglas, Isle of Man.
examples.reason: Douglas datum is distinct from mainland ODN.

examples.scenario: Mainland ODN is applied to St Marys, Scilly.
examples.reason: St Marys has a distinct height datum.

examples.scenario: Mainland ODN is assumed for Orkney without region check.
examples.reason: OSGM15 includes a separate Orkney datum.

examples.scenario: An offshore location beyond the onshore extension is labelled ordinary ODN.
examples.reason: ODN Offshore is explicitly distinct and lower quality.

examples.scenario: ODN Offshore accuracy is reported as mainland ODN accuracy.
examples.reason: Regional model accuracy must follow the actual datum region.

examples.scenario: 0.008 m OSGM15 model accuracy is reported as guaranteed parcel-cell error.
examples.reason: Transformation-model accuracy is not a deterministic per-cell elevation bound.

examples.scenario: GNSS vertical error is omitted from an uncertainty statement.
examples.reason: OSGM15 model error excludes GNSS heighting error.

examples.scenario: A legacy benchmark agrees closely and replaces OSGM15 output.
examples.reason: OS warns lower-order benchmark heights are not reliably maintained.

examples.scenario: Benchmark subsidence risk is ignored in a mining area.
examples.reason: ODN benchmark physical stability can be compromised.

examples.scenario: A benchmark discrepancy causes OSGM15 to be overwritten.
examples.reason: Benchmark comparison is QA, not permission to mutate the canonical transformation.

examples.scenario: Source height unit is feet but recorded as metres.
examples.reason: Height units must be explicit before transformation.

examples.scenario: Output ODN metre values are scaled a second time.
examples.reason: EPSG:5701 gravity-related height is already in metres.

examples.scenario: Vertical axis sign is inverted because image row direction is downward.
examples.reason: Raster row orientation is unrelated to gravity-related height axis direction.

examples.scenario: Geoid-separation sign is hard-coded from memory.
examples.reason: Operation direction and model convention must define the sign.

examples.scenario: EPSG:7711 is reversed directly although marked non-reversible.
examples.reason: A different reversible alternative must be selected explicitly.

examples.scenario: Forward and reverse transformations use different operation identities.
examples.reason: Direction-specific operation provenance must be recorded.

examples.scenario: WGS84 and ETRS89 are treated as identical without source-realization metadata.
examples.reason: High-accuracy vertical work requires the actual source reference frame.

examples.scenario: OSNet v2009 realization is omitted from source provenance.
examples.reason: EPSG:7711 is tied to ETRS89-GBR OSNet v2009.

examples.scenario: Current PROJ resource is fetched from network during replay without digest pinning.
examples.reason: Remote availability must not silently change terminal bytes.

examples.scenario: OS developer raw grid and PROJ GeoTIFF give different results and difference is ignored.
examples.reason: Independent authoritative implementations must reconcile.

examples.scenario: Grid InQuest II differs from the primary implementation.
examples.reason: A reference implementation mismatch blocks terminal use.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent outputs match but model-file digests differ.
examples.reason: Equal result at one point does not prove identical transformation provenance.

examples.scenario: Model files match but target datum IDs differ.
examples.reason: Exact bytes do not repair a wrong target datum label.

examples.scenario: Regional datum classification differs between primary and independent paths.
examples.reason: Different datum regions can yield different height references.

examples.scenario: Interpolation node set differs but output happens to match.
examples.reason: Bilinear support identity is part of exact replay.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 output is rounded before comparison to DTM cells.
examples.reason: Transformation should retain source precision until the explicit storage/output stage.

examples.scenario: Operation accuracy metadata is used to quantize heights.
examples.reason: Accuracy metadata is not a rounding rule.

examples.scenario: An ODN value is finite but target lies outside the selected model region.
examples.reason: Numeric finiteness does not prove datum applicability.

examples.scenario: A fallback geoid is used when OSGM15 resource is missing.
examples.reason: Missing required model bytes must block terminal execution.

examples.scenario: A simple Helmert transformation is used for centimetre-level National Grid/height work.
examples.reason: OS recommends OSTN15/OSGM15 for higher-accuracy transformation.

examples.scenario: Static OSGM15 QA passes and an actual parcel height is emitted.
examples.reason: No canonical target runtime sampling has executed.

examples.scenario: A fixture coordinate from the OS developer pack is copied to the parcel output.
examples.reason: Worked examples validate implementation only.

examples.scenario: Known ACK blocker is relabelled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second vertical-datum runner is launched.
examples.reason: Continuation contract requires the existing shared runner.

examples.scenario: 99.99 readiness is reported as ODN vertical accuracy.
examples.reason: Source-chain readiness is not a measured geodetic accuracy statistic.

examples.scenario: Batch 83 is reported as final parcel height difference.
examples.reason: Canonical point, exact boundary, immutable DTM and executed vertical transformation are still required.
